title: A directed limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps is spectral, with spectral projections
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). Then $X$ is a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and every projection $p_i$ is spectral: $p_i^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2Z (label lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), stated there for a cofiltered index category; a directed set is the special case used here

proof.text: *Step 1 (a basis of $X$; Tag 0A2P in the directed case).* Claim: the sets $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ with $i\in I$ and $U_i\subseteq X_i$ quasi-compact open form a basis of the topology of $X$, and the intersection of two of them is again of this form. Since the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous, the sets $p_i^{-1}(V)$ ($i\in I$, $V\subseteq X_i$ open) form a subbase, so finite intersections of them form a basis ($X=p_i^{-1}(X_i)$ for any $i$, $I$ being nonempty). Given $p_{i_1}^{-1}(V_1),\dots,p_{i_n}^{-1}(V_n)$, $n\ge1$, choose $k\in I$ with $k\ge i_1,\dots,i_n$ ($I$ directed); as $p_{i_l}=f_{i_lk}\circ p_k$ we get $\bigcap_lp_{i_l}^{-1}(V_l)=p_k^{-1}(V)$ with $V=\bigcap_lf_{i_lk}^{-1}(V_l)$ open in $X_k$. So every open $W\subseteq X$ is a union of sets $p_k^{-1}(V)$ with $V\subseteq X_k$ open, and writing each such $V$ as a union of quasi-compact opens of $X_k$ (they form a basis of the spectral space $X_k$), $W$ is a union of sets $p_k^{-1}(U_k)$ with $U_k$ quasi-compact open. For two such sets $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$, $p_j^{-1}(U_j)$ choose $k\ge i,j$: then $p_i^{-1}(U_i)\cap p_j^{-1}(U_j)=p_k^{-1}(f_{ik}^{-1}(U_i)\cap f_{jk}^{-1}(U_j))$, and $f_{ik}^{-1}(U_i)$, $f_{jk}^{-1}(U_j)$ are quasi-compact open ($f_{ik},f_{jk}$ spectral), so their intersection is quasi-compact open ($X_k$ is quasi-separated).

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2P (lemma-describe-limits, line 2374), proof of (1), as quoted in the second paragraph of the proof of 0A2Z

proof.text: *Step 2 (the basic opens and $X$ are quasi-compact; Tag 0A2V and Stacks' 'formal argument').* Fix $i\in I$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$. For $j\in I$ put $Z_j=f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ if $j\ge i$ and $Z_j=X_j$ otherwise. Each $Z_j$ is closed in the constructible topology of $X_j$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]: $X_j$ is; and for $j\ge i$ the set $f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ is a quasi-compact open of $X_j$ ($f_{ij}$ spectral), so its complement is a member of the subbase of the constructible topology, i.e. $f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ is constructibly closed. For $j\le j'$ we have $f_{jj'}(Z_{j'})\subseteq Z_j$: if $j\not\ge i$ this is trivial; if $j\ge i$ then $j'\ge i$ and $f_{ij}\circ f_{jj'}=f_{ij'}$ gives $f_{jj'}(f_{ij'}^{-1}(U_i))\subseteq f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-constructible-closed-quasi-compact] (a directed set is a preordered set) the subset $Z=\{x\in X:p_j(x)\in Z_j\ \forall j\}$ is quasi-compact. But $Z=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$: for $x\in X$ and $j\ge i$, $p_j(x)\in f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ iff $p_i(x)=f_{ij}(p_j(x))\in U_i$, and $j=i$ is among these. So $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ is quasi-compact. The same lemma with $Z_j=X_j$ for all $j$ shows that $X$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), first and second paragraphs

proof.text: *Step 3 (every quasi-compact open of $X$ comes from some $X_k$; Tag 0A2Y, case of a quasi-compact open).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open. By Step 1, $U$ is a union of sets $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ with $U_i\subseteq X_i$ quasi-compact open, and by quasi-compactness of $U$ finitely many suffice: $U=\bigcup_{l=1}^np_{i_l}^{-1}(U_l)$. If $n=0$ then $U=\emptyset=p_i^{-1}(\emptyset)$ for any $i\in I$. Otherwise choose $k\ge i_1,\dots,i_n$ and put $U_k=\bigcup_lf_{i_lk}^{-1}(U_l)$; it is a finite union of quasi-compact opens ($f_{i_lk}$ spectral), hence quasi-compact open, and $p_k^{-1}(U_k)=\bigcup_l(f_{i_lk}\circ p_k)^{-1}(U_l)=\bigcup_lp_{i_l}^{-1}(U_l)=U$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Y (lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-constructible, line 4862), first paragraph, cited in the third paragraph of the proof of 0A2Z

proof.text: *Step 4 (quasi-compact, quasi-separated, basis of quasi-compact opens; $p_i$ spectral).* $X$ is quasi-compact (Step 2). The quasi-compact opens of $X$ form a basis: the basis of Step 1 consists of opens that are quasi-compact by Step 2. If $U,U'\subseteq X$ are quasi-compact open, Step 3 writes them as $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and $p_j^{-1}(U_j)$ with quasi-compact opens $U_i,U_j$; by Step 1 $U\cap U'=p_k^{-1}(U_k)$ with $U_k\subseteq X_k$ quasi-compact open, which is quasi-compact by Step 2. Finally for every $i$ and every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$, $p_i^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact (Step 2), and $p_i$ is continuous: $p_i$ is spectral.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), second and third paragraphs

proof.text: *Step 5 (existence of a generic point).* Let $Z\subseteq X$ be an irreducible closed subset [def-weil-irreducible-components]. For $i\in I$, $p_i(Z)$ is irreducible [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-continuous-image], so its closure $Z_i=\overline{p_i(Z)}$ is an irreducible closed subset of $X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure] and has a unique generic point $\xi_i$ ($X_i$ is spectral, hence sober [def-weil-spectral-space]). For $i\le j$: the closed set $f_{ij}^{-1}(Z_i)$ contains $p_j(Z)$ (as $f_{ij}\circ p_j=p_i$), hence $Z_j$, so $f_{ij}(\xi_j)\in Z_i$ and $\overline{\{f_{ij}(\xi_j)\}}\subseteq Z_i$; conversely the closed set $f_{ij}^{-1}(\overline{\{f_{ij}(\xi_j)\}})$ contains $\xi_j$, hence $Z_j=\overline{\{\xi_j\}}\supseteq p_j(Z)$, so $\overline{\{f_{ij}(\xi_j)\}}\supseteq f_{ij}(p_j(Z))=p_i(Z)$ and, being closed, $\supseteq Z_i$. Thus $f_{ij}(\xi_j)$ is a generic point of $Z_i$ and $f_{ij}(\xi_j)=\xi_i$. By the description of the points of $X$ there is $\xi\in X$ with $p_i(\xi)=\xi_i$ for all $i$. Claim $\xi\in Z$: otherwise $X\setminus Z$ is an open neighbourhood of $\xi$, so by Step 1 it contains some $p_i^{-1}(U_i)\ni\xi$ with $U_i$ quasi-compact open; then $\xi_i\in U_i$, so the open $U_i$ meets $Z_i=\overline{p_i(Z)}$ and therefore meets $p_i(Z)$, i.e. $p_i(z)\in U_i$ for some $z\in Z$, and $z\in p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq X\setminus Z$, a contradiction. So $\overline{\{\xi\}}\subseteq Z$ ($Z$ closed). Conversely let $z\in Z$ and $W$ an open neighbourhood of $z$; by Step 1 $z\in p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq W$ for some $i$ and open $U_i$. Then $p_i(z)\in U_i\cap Z_i$, so the open $U_i$ meets $Z_i=\overline{\{\xi_i\}}$, hence contains $\xi_i$, hence $\xi\in p_i^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq W$. So $z\in\overline{\{\xi\}}$, and $\overline{\{\xi\}}=Z$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), fourth paragraph

proof.text: *Step 6 (uniqueness of the generic point, omitted in Stacks; conclusion).* Let $\eta\in Z$ be a second point with $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Z$, and $i\in I$. Then $p_i(\eta)\in p_i(Z)\subseteq Z_i$, so $\overline{\{p_i(\eta)\}}\subseteq Z_i$; and the closed set $p_i^{-1}(\overline{\{p_i(\eta)\}})$ contains $\eta$, hence $Z$, so $\overline{\{p_i(\eta)\}}\supseteq p_i(Z)$ and therefore $\supseteq Z_i$. Thus $p_i(\eta)$ is a generic point of $Z_i$, and by uniqueness in the spectral space $X_i$, $p_i(\eta)=\xi_i=p_i(\xi)$. This holds for every $i$, and $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is injective, so $\eta=\xi$. Hence every irreducible closed subset of $X$ has a unique generic point, and with Step 4 $X$ is a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] whose projections $p_i$ are spectral.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), last paragraph: Stacks omits the uniqueness and gives the hint written out here
